claims.text: The starting material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Uncoated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
A thin, diffusion-bonded aluminide coating can be applied to as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by pack cementation or a similar surface-modification method.
The aluminide coating provides an aluminum reservoir at the alloy surface.
During high-temperature exposure, the aluminide coating will form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface film.
The aluminide layer reacts with oxygen at elevated temperature to form Al2O3.
The resulting Al2O3 scale is stable and slow-growing.
The Al2O3 scale protects the underlying HfNbTaTiZr from further oxidation.
A thin aluminide coating will leave the alloy's bulk microstructure largely unaltered.
Leaving the bulk microstructure largely unaltered will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
At approximately 1000 °C in air for up to about 100 hours, the coated alloy will have markedly lower oxidation weight gain than the uncoated alloy.
At approximately 1000 °C in air for up to about 100 hours, the coated alloy will develop a thinner oxide scale than the uncoated alloy.
After coating and exposure, tensile ductility will remain similar to that of uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
After coating and exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C will remain similar to that of uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed operating boundary is air at around 1000 °C for approximately 100 hours, with high-temperature strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
A reduction greater than 15% in either ductility or yield strength relative to the uncoated control is defined as mechanical falsification.

contradictions.description: The conditions include static or cyclic mechanical loading, but the uncertainty statement describes performance beyond tested static conditions as unknown. It is therefore unclear whether cyclic loading is actually within the proposed test boundary.
